paragraphs.en: Scientific publishing has long been a licence to print money. Scientists need journals in which to publish their research, so they will supply the articles without monetary reward. Other scientists perform the specialised work of peer review also for free, because it is a central element in the acquisition of status and the production of scientific knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 长期以来，科学出版业一直如同获得了印钞许可。科学家需要期刊来发表研究，因此愿意无偿提供论文。其他科学家也免费承担同行评审这一专业工作，因为它是获得学术地位、生产科学知识的核心环节。

paragraphs.en: With the content of papers secured for free, the publisher needs only find a market for its journal. Until this century, university libraries were not very price sensitive. Scientific publishers routinely report profit margins approaching 40% on their operations at a time when the rest of the publishing industry is in an existential crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 既然免费获得了论文内容，出版商只需为期刊找到市场即可。在本世纪到来之前，大学图书馆对价格并不十分敏感。在出版业其他领域面临生存危机之际，科学出版商却经常报告其业务利润率接近40%。

paragraphs.en: The Dutch giant Elsevier, which claims to publish 25% of the scientific papers produced in the world, made profits of more than £900m last year, while UK universities alone spent more than £210m in 2016 to enable researchers to access their own publicly funded research; both figures seem to rise unstoppably despite increasingly desperate efforts to change them.
paragraphs.zh: 荷兰出版巨头爱思唯尔声称，全球25%的科学论文由其出版。该公司去年获利超过9亿英镑；而仅英国各大学在2016年就花费了超过2.1亿英镑，使研究人员能够查阅他们自己依靠公共资金完成的研究。尽管人们正以越来越迫切的努力试图改变这种局面，这两个数字似乎仍在不可阻挡地上升。

paragraphs.en: The most drastic, an thoroughly illegal, reaction has been the emergence of Sci-Hub, a kind of global photocopier for scientific papers, set up in 2012, which now claims to offer access to every paywalled article published since 2015. The success of Sci-Hub, which relies on researchers passing on copies they have themselves legally accessed, shows the legal ecosystem has lost legitimacy among its users and must be transformed so that it works for all participants.
paragraphs.zh: 最激烈、同时也完全违法的应对方式，是Sci-Hub的出现。它于2012年建立，像一台面向全球科学论文的复印机，如今声称能够提供2015年以来发表的每一篇付费论文。Sci-Hub依赖研究人员转交他们自己合法获取的论文副本；它的成功表明，现有合法生态体系已经失去了用户对其正当性的认可，必须加以改造，使其能够为所有参与者服务。

paragraphs.en: In Britain the move towards open access publishing has been driven by funding bodies. In some ways it has been very successful. More than half of all British scientific research is now published under open access terms: either freely available from the moment of publication, or paywalled for a year or more so that the publishers can make a profit before being placed on general release.
paragraphs.zh: 在英国，向开放获取出版模式的转变一直由资助机构推动。在某些方面，这一转变取得了很大成功。如今，英国超过一半的科学研究成果都按照开放获取条款发表：要么从发表之时起就可免费获取，要么先付费开放一年或更久，让出版商获得利润，然后再向公众免费开放。

paragraphs.en: Yet the new system has not yet worked out any cheaper for the universities. Publishers have responded to the demand that they make their product free to readers by charging their writers fees to cover the costs of prep ring an article. These range from around £500 to $5,000, and apparently the work gets more expensive the more that publishers do it. A report last year pointed out that the costs both of subscriptions and of these “article preparation costs” had been steadily rising at a rate above inflation.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这一新体系迄今并未给大学节省费用。面对要求向读者免费提供产品的呼声，出版商的回应是向作者收费，以支付论文出版准备工作的成本。这类费用从约500英镑到5000美元不等，而且出版商做这项工作的次数越多，费用显然反而越高。去年的一份报告指出，订阅费和这些“论文准备费”一直在以超过通货膨胀的速度稳步上涨。

paragraphs.en: In some ways the scientific publishing model resembles the economy of the social internet: labour is provided free in exchange for the hope of status, while huge profits are made by a few big firms who run the market places. In both cases, we need a rebalancing of power.
paragraphs.zh: 在某些方面，科学出版模式类似于社交互联网的经济模式：人们为获得地位的希望而无偿付出劳动，运营交易平台的少数大公司则赚取巨额利润。在这两种情形中，我们都需要重新平衡各方的权力。
